meta.title: Manifesto · Dentalpin
meta.description: Why Dentalpin exists and what we promise the dental industry: open, modular, calm software. For clinics who've been waiting years for something better.

manifestoPage.title: No clinic should be held hostage by its software.
manifestoPage.lead: We've been working alongside the dental sector for years and we know what software has given it: clinics that invoice, schedule and pull up patient histories in seconds where there used to be paper and phone calls. But that first generation can't stretch any further: interfaces that haven't been rethought in fifteen years, migrations that turn impossible the moment a clinic wants to grow, data that's painful to export, and licensing models that fit some clinics and suffocate others. The sector is ready for a new leap, one that keeps the wins of the previous generation and adds everything 2026 makes possible. This manifesto is our way of pushing that leap, with respect for what has been built and ambition for what's still missing.

sections.heading: What we've been seeing for years
sections.body: We see dentists lean on their management software for years to remember appointments, keep patient histories and invoice with rigour. What feels obvious today is something those programs won. But we also see those same professionals open the screen and sense the day is about to run slower, receptionists who hang up the phone to wrestle a search box, owners who find out that exporting their own database costs a four-figure invoice and a six-week wait. It isn't that the sector chose badly, it's that the alternative hadn't been built yet. Until now.

sections.heading: What we believe
sections.body: We believe in free software, and in the idea that there should exist an open alternative where a clinic can manage its patients' data. We believe a program a hygienist will open fifty times a day deserves to be beautiful, fast and well designed. We believe a clinic owner should be able to decide whether to keep their data in the cloud or on a server inside the clinic. We believe code that handles health data should be readable, auditable and discussable in broad daylight. We believe AI will transform this sector, for the better, only if it's built with humans at the wheel. And we believe no dentist in Santiago, Bogotá, New York, Madrid or Lisbon should wait five years for software to "reach their market".

sections.heading: What we promise you
sections.body: We won't sell you plans or per-user seats. We won't raise your price when you grow. We won't hide features behind "contact sales". We won't lock you into our servers. We won't close the source when things go well. And we promise that what you use today will still exist tomorrow. Because it lives on GitHub, because anyone can keep it alive, because it doesn't depend on us staying around.

sections.heading: What we ask from you
sections.body: If you like Dentalpin and it saves you a few hours this week, tell another clinic. If you find a bug, open an issue on GitHub. If you're missing a module, describe it and someone (you, us or the community) will build it. If you speak another language, translate it. If you try it and it's not for you, write us with all the love in the world: feedback makes us better. This isn't a company selling you a product. It's a community building the infrastructure a whole sector needs.

sections.heading: Where we're going
sections.body: We want that, in five years, opening a new clinic will be about deciding what to do with your patients, not which software to avoid. We want the next generation of dentists to learn on a system that helps them and respects their time. We want dental practice management software to stop being a problem and to finally become, at last, invisible, like electricity or hot water.

manifestoPage.closing: This is Dentalpin. If you've read this far, you might never look at your clinic's software the same way again.

meta.title: Technology · Dentalpin
meta.description: How Dentalpin is built underneath: plugin architecture, anatomy of a module, and the stack that holds it all together.

techPage.title: The stack you'd pick if you could start from scratch.
techPage.lead: Dentalpin isn't a black box. Everything that makes it tick lives on GitHub and is documented: a small core, modules that plug in, a stack serious teams pick, and no hidden magic.

principles.title: Four decisions that run the codebase.

items.title: Small core, modules that plug in
items.body: The core owns auth, RBAC, clinics and users. Everything else lives as a module, installable and removable without touching the rest.

items.title: Contracts before classes
items.body: Each module ships typed events and Pydantic endpoints. Other modules react to events, not to internal imports.

items.title: API first, UI after
items.body: Everything you see in the interface goes through the same public API that integrators and AI agents already use.

items.title: A deliberately boring stack
items.body: We pick tools with years of production behind them. Exotic stays in side projects.

anatomy.title: What every module ships inside.
anatomy.body: A module isn't an improvised plugin. It follows a clear contract so Dentalpin recognises it and the rest of the system can build on top.

items.name: manifest.yaml
items.what: Name, version, dependencies, permissions and events it publishes or listens to.

items.name: Alembic migrations
items.what: Its own migration branch. Enabling the module applies its tables, disabling leaves them in place until you decide.

items.name: YAML seeds
items.what: Sample data and base catalogues so you can boot the module without hand-writing SQL.

items.name: Auto-registered navigation
items.what: The module declares its menu entries and routes. The UI only shows them when the role has permission.

items.name: Event bus
items.what: Subscribes to core or other modules' events and publishes its own. That's the glue between pieces.

items.name: FastAPI endpoints
items.what: Every module domain exposed as public API, typed with Pydantic and documented with OpenAPI.

meta.title: Verifactu for dental clinics · Dentalpin
meta.description: Optional Spain-only module: comply with Veri*Factu (RD 1007/2023, Orden HAC/1177/2024) without changing your invoicing flow. Mandatory from January 2027.

verifactuPage.title: Verifactu, ready for 2027.
verifactuPage.tagline: The module that meets Veri*Factu without anyone on your team noticing.
verifactuPage.lead: From January 1st, 2027, every clinic in Spain that issues an invoice must submit it to AEAT in real time. Verifactu does it for you, without changing how you invoice today. Turn the module on, configure it once, forget it.

deadlineHero.label: MANDATORY
deadlineHero.footnote: Voluntary phase open since 2026 with no penalties for technical errors.

what.title: A new legal duty. One module that resolves it.
what.body: Veri*Factu is the AEAT regime that forces every invoicing system in Spain (the SIFs) to record each issued invoice in a signed chain and submit it to the tax authority in near real time. Whoever invoices must comply. Whoever builds the software must adapt it. Dentalpin ships this as an optional module, ready for your clinic to switch on whenever you want.

items.title: SHA-256 hash chain
items.body: Every invoice produces a record that links to the previous one. The chain becomes an append-only fiscal ledger no operator can tamper with without breaking the hash.

items.title: Signed AEAT submission
items.body: Your FNMT certificate signs every SOAP envelope over mTLS. Pre-production and production swap with one click, no redeploy.

items.title: Verifiable PDF QR
items.body: Every invoice ships with a QR that any patient can scan and validate on AEAT’s public portal.

timeline.title: What your clinic must have ready, and when.
timeline.body: The Veri*Factu transition is not an event, it’s a calendar. These are the dates that matter.

items.label: Done
items.title: Software vendors (SIFs) enter voluntary mode.
items.body: Dentalpin already ships real submissions to AEAT pre-production from this date.

items.label: Now
items.title: Voluntary phase, no penalties for technical errors.
items.body: The right window to enable Verifactu, validate it against pre-production and leave your chain ready.

items.label: Mandatory
items.title: Companies (Impuesto sobre Sociedades): mandatory.
items.body: Any clinic taxed under IS must submit invoices to AEAT from day one of the year.

items.label: Mandatory
items.title: Self-employed, IRPF and others: mandatory.
items.body: The remaining payers go live six months later. Before that date, your clinic should already have Verifactu running with a real certificate.

flow.title: Sits below your invoicing. Without touching your flow.
flow.body: Your team invoices as always. Verifactu only kicks in at issue time and brings the invoice into compliance before you finish printing it.

steps.title: You issue the invoice
steps.body: You hit "Issue" in Dentalpin. The module builds the RegistroAlta payload with all AEAT-mandated fields.

steps.title: Hash is computed
steps.body: SHA-256 linking this invoice to the previous one. The record enters the chain in pending state.

steps.title: QR + huella returned
steps.body: Before printing the PDF, Verifactu returns the hash, the tax-QR URL and the invoice type. Your PDF is born compliant.

steps.title: Worker submits to AEAT
steps.body: Every 60 s, a worker drains pending records, signs the SOAP envelope with your FNMT certificate over mTLS and ships them in batches up to 1,000.

steps.title: AEAT replies
steps.body: The module parses the response, updates the state (Correct, AcceptedWithErrors, Incorrect) and stores AEAT’s CSV receipt in the record.

setup.title: Five guided steps. One time only.
setup.body: The module ships with a checklist panel in the back office. Each step shows green, amber or red and blocks activation until everything is ready.

steps.title: Clinic identity
steps.body: Tax ID and legal name. Verifactu reads them from the clinic record so no fiscal data is duplicated.

steps.title: FNMT digital certificate
steps.body: You upload your .pfx with the password. It’s stored encrypted with Fernet. The UI shows expiry and warns near renewal.

steps.title: SIF producer
steps.body: A wizard with an electronically-signed declaración responsable. After signing you can download the signed PDF for your archive or for AEAT inspections.

steps.title: VAT to AEAT mapping
steps.body: Each catalog VAT type maps to its AEAT classification (S1 standard, E1 health-services exemption, N1 non-taxable…). The module seeds E1 by default for 0% types (clinical services).

steps.title: Activate the module
steps.body: When all four steps are green, the "Activate Verifactu" button lights up. You start in test (AEAT pre-production) and switch to production whenever you’re ready.

compare.title: Test and live, hot-swappable.
compare.body: Same module, two endpoints. Switch with a click. No data migration, no reinstall.

rows.test: Real FNMT or AEAT test cert

compare.footnote: Switching `prod → test` doesn’t break the local chain (it’s global per NIF), but AEAT will see a gap in whichever environment you skip.

datamodel.title: Four tables. Zero columns added to anything else.
datamodel.body: Verifactu lives in its own space. It reads from clinics and catalog, but never adds columns. Uninstall it (with no accepted records) and you’re back to before, with no trace.

tables.name: verifactu_settings
tables.what: One row per clinic. State, environment, producer NIF, chain head, send-window timings.

tables.name: verifactu_certificates
tables.what: Encrypted PFX + password vault using Fernet. Subject CN, holder NIF and validity dates power the expiry banner.

tables.name: verifactu_records
tables.what: Append-only fiscal ledger. Verbatim XML, hash, previous hash, AEAT state and response CSV. Retained 4 years per LGT.

tables.name: verifactu_vat_classifications
tables.what: Per-clinic mapping S1/E1–E6/N1/N2 by VAT type. Keeps the Dentalpin catalog country-agnostic.

isolation.title: A country module. Not a fork of the product.
isolation.body: Dentalpin is international software. Veri*Factu is Spain. The boundary is sharp: the module wires into `BillingHookRegistry` only when `clinic.settings.country == "ES"`, never touches billing or catalog tables and disappears without aftermath when uninstalled.

items.title: Modular and optional
items.body: Not installed by default. Clinics outside Spain see zero extra screens; Spanish ones turn it on from Admin → Modules.

items.title: Isolated by design
items.body: All its tables live with `verifactu_*` prefixes. No Spanish fiscal columns leak into the core; no core module speaks AEAT.

items.title: Reusable as a pattern
items.body: Tomorrow `factur-x-fr` for France or `sdi-it` for Italy ship with the same shape. Each country owns its complexity.

queue.title: When something goes wrong, you see it where it should be.
queue.body: If AEAT rejects a submission or the network fails, the issue surfaces in the queue and is retried for you. You see the real codes with their legal description, not generic ones.

tabs.label: Pending
tabs.body: Records in pending or sending state. The worker processes them every 60 seconds.

tabs.label: Rejected
tabs.body: AEAT business rejection (Incorrect). Shows the exact code, description and a "Retry (Subsanación)" button that resends with `Subsanacion=S` and `RechazoPrevio=X`.

tabs.label: Transient errors
tabs.body: Transport failures or AEAT outages. The worker retries on its own with exponential back-off.

penalties.title: The price of not being ready by January 2027.
penalties.body: Spain’s LGT 201 bis governs liability for using non-compliant SIFs. Fines can reach €50,000 per fiscal year. For a clinic that invoices every day, skipping Verifactu (or an equivalent) stops being an option.

items.title: For your clinic
items.body: Fines for using non-homologated software. Risk continues for as long as you keep issuing non-compliant invoices.

items.title: For your accountant
items.body: Tighter inspections and mandatory traceability of every invoice. Veri*Factu turns accountants into reviewers, not capturers.

items.title: For your patient
items.body: The QR on the invoice lets them verify the expense is logged with AEAT, which is often required for health insurance reimbursements.

items.q: Do I need to enable it now?
items.a: No. If your clinic is taxed under Sociedades, the deadline is January 1st, 2027. If you’re self-employed (IRPF) it’s July 1st, 2027. Until then you’re in voluntary mode with no penalties for technical errors. The best time to enable it is now and let it run against pre-production.

The module is Spain only. If your clinic doesn’t invoice in Spain, you’ll never see it: it’s not installed by default. For France and other countries we plan sibling modules (factur-x, SDI…) that plug in the same way.

items.q: What do I need to start?
items.a: Three things: (1) your CIF/NIF in the clinic record, (2) a valid FNMT certificate (Representante de Persona Jurídica, Persona Física or Sello de Empresa) and (3) decide who signs the producer’s declaración responsable (the SaaS, your integrator or your clinic if you self-host).

items.q: What about invoices issued before activation?
items.a: They don’t flow into Verifactu retroactively: the chain starts the day you enable the module. The law only requires new invoices to be signed and submitted. Older ones remain legally valid.

items.q: What happens if AEAT goes down?
items.a: Verifactu marks records as transient errors and retries on its own every 60 seconds with back-off. Your clinic keeps invoicing as usual: submissions complete when AEAT comes back.
Yes, while you have no accepted records. Once a single Correct record exists, you must keep the chain for four years (LGT). The back office tells you before letting you uninstall.

items.q: Do partial payments and credit notes work?
items.a: Yes. F1, F2, F3 and every credit note R1–R5 are supported, plus anulaciones (RegistroAnulacion). Simplified invoices capped at €400 with no recipient are validated.

items.q: Can I verify an issued invoice from outside?
items.a: Yes. The PDF QR points to AEAT’s `ValidarQR` URL. Anyone can scan it and confirm the invoice is registered.

callout.title: Does your clinic invoice in Spain? You’re a click away from being 2027-ready.
callout.body: Verifactu is an optional module bundled with Dentalpin. It complies with RD 1007/2023, signs every invoice and submits it to AEAT in real time. Turn it on whenever you want and have it ready before the deadline.
